messages:
incident-bot: [SEV2] High error rate observed on hosted inference (eu-west-1). Routing 5xx spike > 12% over baseline 00:10. Paging oncall-tim and sre-ana. Links: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/alerts/3276543210 :rotating_light:

oncall-tim: Acknowledged. seeing large latency and 5xx on /v1/generate. Dashboard shows a rapid scale up of GPU pods then a lot of CrashLoopBackOff.

sre-ana: grabbing logs now. initial hypothesis: autoscaler reacted to latency, scaled up with a new node group, but new pods are hitting CUDA OOM and restarting — causing more load to remaining pods -> more scale -> thrash.

infra-jia: confirming nodes: new-pool-eu-2 started 6 instances at 01:09, pods scheduled there and immediate restarts. dmesg on node-7 shows repeated CUDA memory faults.

ml-mohammed: logs from model-worker: ```
I0325 01:10:31.123 model-worker.cpp:450] Allocating KV cache 14.5GB
E0325 01:10:31.456 cuda_driver.cpp:78] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1536MB
E0325 01:10:31.457 container_runtime.cpp:212] Process exited with code 137
```

support-lina: Customer-impact: multiple customers in EU reported 500s and partial responses. Support ticket influx up ~4x. Flagging Enterprise customers A & B.

oncall-tim: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler scale-ups. 2) Force fallback to smaller model variant for new requests. 3) Cordon/drain problematic nodes. 4) Reduce concurrent model instances per pod. Who can flip autoscaler? @infra-jia?

infra-jia: I can pause the autoscaler policy. Running: `kubectl patch hpa inference-autoscaler -n redwood -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 10, "maxReplicas": 10}}'` to pin capacity while we triage. Doing it now.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: paused new autoscale policy rollout (build #2024) by request of infra-jia.

oncall-tim: Good. @ml-mohammed can you push a traffic-split to route new sessions to `redwood/gpt-eco-v1` (smaller mem footprint) and enable cache-prefill for hot prefixes? Command we use: `curl -X POST https://api.console.local/v1/traffic-split -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"gpt-eco-v1"}'`

ml-mohammed: Doing traffic split, will route 100% of new non-enterprise traffic to gpt-eco-v1. Enterprise customers kept on pinned capacity for now. Done in ~30s.

sre-ana: I'm seeing error rate drop to ~6% now for general traffic but still 500s for some pinned enterprise routes because they land on pinned nodes that are flapping. We'll drain the worst offending nodes. @infra-jia can you identify nodes with repeated `ContainerExitCode=137`?

infra-jia: Node list with OOM restarts: node-7, node-8, node-9. Starting `kubectl cordon node-7 && kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now. Draining node-8 next.

support-lina: Noting customer B (EU-3) complaints: degraded inference quality due to fallback model; ETA on full restoration?

oncall-tim: Goal: stop the thrash and stabilize within 30 minutes, then reopen capacity in controlled increments. We need a follow-up for customer communication: @product-casey can you draft a short status note for EU customers: impact, mitigation (fallback model + reduced throughput), ETA and next steps? Keep it factual + blameless.

product-casey: On it. Draft: "We experienced degraded inference availability in eu-west-1 starting 01:08. We've applied a temporary traffic split to a lower-memory model variant and pinned capacity to prevent further autoscaling thrash. Enterprise pinned routes may still see residual 500s while we drain affected nodes. We expect stabilization within 30-45 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary." Will post after review.

ml-mohammed: Quick dev note: root cause appears to be a new model packaging change in the last canary that increased GPU memory footprint by ~2GB due to a pre-initialized KV cache. When combined with high concurrency this pushes pods over device memory and triggers OOMs. Canary rolled out by build #2024.

oncall-tim: Good catch. @deploy-bot when did build #2024 go to canary?

deploy-bot: build #2024 promoted to canary eu-west at 00:58 by ci-user. Canary set size: 10 pods.

sre-ana: Action items (live):
- [x] Pin autoscaler to fixed capacity (infra-jia)
- [x] Route non-enterprise traffic to gpt-eco-v1 (ml-mohammed)
- [x] Drain flapping nodes node-7/8/9 (infra-jia)
- [ ] Roll back canary build #2024 from canary and scale up verified build #2019
- [ ] Postmortem, include quant metrics: model memory delta, autoscaler settings, HPA damping/scaleDown stabilization seconds

infra-jia: Canary rollback in progress: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-worker --to-revision=2019 -n redwood` then scaling stable pods. Doing that now.

ml-mohammed: Rolling back model artifact and clearing prefill KV cache on workers. Will monitor memory usage.

oncall-tim: After rollback, we should slowly increase `maxReplicas` with a large `scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds` to avoid re-trigger. Who can update HPA to set `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` and `scaleDown: 0.2`?

infra-jia: I'll update the autoscaler policy to add damping: `spec.behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` and `scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` patched. Pushing now.

support-lina: Customer comms posted to status page and sent to queued enterprise contacts. Notified CS for individual follow-ups.

product-casey: Updated status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3276543210 — includes mitigation steps and ETA.

sre-ana: Post-rollback metrics look good. Error rate down to ~1.2%, latency back to baseline for non-enterprise routes. Enterprise pinned routes gradually recovering as drained nodes evacuated.

oncall-tim: Good. Transitioning to monitoring phase. I'll stay on call for 30m. @sre-ana please own postmortem writeup and include timeline + actionable items: increase canary validation for memory, add pre-deploy test that measures model RAM at startup, and change autoscaler to prefer vertical throttle (queueing) vs aggressive horizontal up.

ml-mohammed: Also propose to change model packaging to lazy-init KV cache and add a preflight check to abort rollout if mem delta > 500MB.

infra-jia: Will uncordon nodes after we confirm no regressions and replace faulty instances with updated AMI.

support-lina: I'll update customers in 45m with follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to "Mitigated" at 01:47. Tagging for postmortem: owner=sre-ana, severity=SEV2, duration=39m.

oncall-tim: Thanks all. Document the exact autoscaler settings we pinned and the canary revision numbers in the incident doc. Handoff to sre-ana for postmortem. If anyone has leftover actions, add them to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
